record.paper_title: Aspects of Semiclassical Black Holes: Development and Open Problems
record.original_question: In multimessenger observations of compact objects, can naked singularities be distinguished from astrophysical black holes by their observational signatures, including changes in neighboring geometry, energetic photons from the high-density region, deviations from classical geodesic motion, accretion-disk luminosity or flux, photon-ring bending, particle-collision patterns, or high-frequency gravitational-wave deviations?

evidence.quote: observational signatures of such exotic objects

artifact.status_search_result: Multiple theoretical studies have established partial distinguishing criteria: naked singularities without photon spheres produce qualitatively different shadow/photon-ring structures, brighter and harder accretion-disk spectra, modified ISCO and frame-dragging, and altered particle-collision and GW signatures compared with Kerr/Schwarzschild black holes. However, naked-singularity models possessing a photon sphere can closely mimic black-hole images, and no observation to date has provided a decisive discrimination. The problem of a complete and observationally conclusive distinction therefore remains open in general, while partial signatures are known.

status_evidence.title: Observational signatures of strongly naked singularities: image of the thin accretion disk
status_evidence.snippet: Naked singularities lacking a photon sphere produce a complex structure of bright rings absent in Schwarzschild black holes.
status_evidence.claim: Imaging of thin accretion disks can distinguish strongly naked singularities from black holes in specific cases.

status_evidence.title: Distinguishing black holes from naked singularities through their accretion disk properties
status_evidence.snippet: Disks around naked singularities are much more luminous, with a high-frequency power-law spectral component.
status_evidence.claim: Accretion-disk luminosity and spectra provide a partial discriminator.

status_evidence.title: Distinguishing Brans–Dicke–Kerr naked singularities and black holes via thin-disk EM radiation
status_evidence.snippet: Comparison of thin disk electromagnetic radiation properties differentiates Brans-Dicke-Kerr naked singularities from Kerr black holes.
status_evidence.claim: Specific naked-singularity families admit electromagnetic discriminators, but a generic resolution is not established.
